title: 3D Perspective Battle Stage
description: The central battle stage renders Pokémon Showdown battles in full 3D perspective with official animated battle sprites (fully supporting all regional variants, alternate forms, Mega Evolutions, and Gen 9 species), HP gauges with color-transition fills, status condition badges, stat stage counters, and a 6-pokeball team health tracker.
steps: 1. Observe the top-right section to inspect Trainer 2's active Pokémon and remaining team Pokéballs.
2. Observe the bottom-left section to inspect Trainer 1's active Pokémon and team Pokéballs.
3. Active field conditions (Sun, Rain, Sandstorm, Snow, Electric Terrain, Grassy Terrain) appear as floating status badges at the top center of the battlefield.

4. Active move announcement banners float across the stadium indicating which Pokémon is attacking, the move used, and effectiveness (Super Effective / Resisted / Critical Hit) with synchronized lunge and hit-shake animations.
5. In Manual Mode, an interactive Action HUD appears at the bottom with move options and bench switches.

title: Real-Time Advantage Bar
description: Located directly below the battle field, this dynamic bar displays live match balance and win probabilities for Trainer 1 vs Trainer 2 calculated from remaining team HP percentage, alive Pokémon counts, and active type matchups.
steps: 1. Check the left and right percentages to see Trainer 1 and Trainer 2 calculated win probability.
2. Read the center numerical badge (+1.5 for Trainer 1 advantage, -2.0 for Trainer 2 advantage).
3. As Pokémon take damage or faint, the advantage bar smoothly animates to reflect the shift in momentum.
4. When the battlefield orientation is flipped using the Flip button, the advantage bar automatically inverts to match the perspective of the bottom trainer.

title: Controls Card & Match Modes
description: The controls card features a single-row cyberpunk glassmorphism layout with mode selection dropdown, primary battle action controls, and secondary utility icon buttons.
steps: 1. Open the Mode dropdown on the left to switch between 'Automated Match' (continuous AI battle) and 'Manual Mode' (interactive play).
2. In Automated Match, use the primary Play button to Start, Pause/Resume, or Stop the match loop.
3. In Manual Mode, use the glowing Step AI button to trigger a step-by-step turn execution.

4. Use the right-hand utility icon buttons to adjust Speed (turn delay), Reset the battle with fresh teams, Flip the battlefield orientation between Trainer 1 and Trainer 2, Copy the battle log to clipboard, or Export the log to a text file.

title: Player Cards & Full Team Roster
description: Streamlined cards for Player 1, Player 2, and Decision model display names, in-card model selection dropdowns, live turn status, and full 6-Pokémon team rosters with interactive health gauges, status conditions, and detailed moveset/item/ability tooltips.
steps: 1. Inspect the 6-Pokémon squad directly inside each Player card to monitor HP percentages, active field status, and fainted states in real-time.
2. Hover over any Pokémon chip to view its full types, current/max HP, ability, held item, and 4 moves.
3. Click any Pokémon chip to open the dedicated Pokémon Detail Modal for deeper statistical analysis.
4. Use the in-card model dropdown to change player AI models instantly without leaving the battle.

title: Custom Teambuilder & Presets
description: Build custom 6-Pokémon competitive teams for Trainer 1 and Trainer 2, import or export standard Showdown text formats (PokePaste compatible), or load battle-tested competitive archetypes.
steps: 1. Click the Edit Teams icon button in the top header to open the Teambuilder modal.
2. Switch between Trainer 1 (P1) and Trainer 2 (P2), or click 'Swap P1/P2' to swap rosters.
3. Load competitive presets: Kanto Legends, Rain Hyper Offense, Sun Power Squad, Paldea OU Titans, Trick Room Titans, or roll a fresh random team.
4. Edit species, items, abilities, Tera types, and movesets in the Visual Grid, or paste raw text in the Showdown Text tab.
5. Click 'Apply & Start Battle' to initiate simulation with your custom teams, or 'Revert to Pure Random Battles' anytime.

title: Middle Decision Model
description: The Decision Model acts as a supervisory Grandmaster battle coach. Native decision models (such as laya:421m-typed-decisions-mlx-fp16) leverage Ollama's high-speed structured /v1/systemone endpoint for sub-second evaluations. When active, it critiques proposed moves, identifies tactical blunders (such as attacking into type immunities or failing to switch from lethal 4x weaknesses), assigns grades, and provides commentary.
steps: 1. Select a decision model inside the Decision Model card in the right column.
2. When a player AI proposes an action, the Decision Model evaluates the play in milliseconds and outputs a grade (Best Move, Tactical Read, Inaccuracy, Blunder).
3. If no decision-capable models are configured, the Decision Model card automatically hides with zero broken UI.

title: Model Providers & Setup
description: Connect to local Ollama models (with automatic CORS proxy, fast-reasoning token suppression, and native /v1/systemone decision model integration), external OpenAI-compatible endpoints, or the built-in Offline Heuristic Engine. Functional-calling, embedding, and non-chat models are automatically excluded to ensure clean turn play.
steps: 1. Click the Settings icon in the header to open the API drawer.
2. Select your provider: Ollama, OpenAI, or Offline.
3. For local Ollama, ensure `ollama serve` is running. Enable 'Fast Reasoning Bypass' for sub-2s responses on reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1 or Qwen 3.5 MLX.
4. Click 'Refresh Models' in the settings drawer or click the interactive refresh icon directly inside the header's Ollama provider pill to re-sync available models at any time.

title: Gen 9 Random Battle Mechanics
description: The simulator executes the official Pokémon Showdown Gen 9 Random Battle format with balanced competitive move pools, abilities, items, and Terastallization mechanics.
steps: 1. Both trainers receive 6 randomly generated competitive Pokémon with balanced levels and moves.
2. Terastallization is available once per battle, shifting the Pokémon's defensive and offensive typing.
3. The battle ends when all 6 Pokémon on one team faint.

title: AI Thoughts Stream
description: The bottom-right card provides a unified, continuous AI Thoughts stream that combines AI model strategic reasoning chains, Decision Model evaluations and grades, and real-time combat events into one synchronized feed.
steps: 1. Inspect each thought card in the stream to see which Player acted, their streamlined move or switch action badge, and their strategic reasoning.
2. Review the Decision Model verdict box with its grade badge (Best Move, Tactical Read, Inaccuracy, Blunder) and tactical critique.
3. Real-time combat outcomes (damage percentages, effectiveness, stat boosts, faints, and weather shifts) appear chronologically in the stream alongside the thoughts.
4. The counter badge in the card header tracks total AI decisions, and the stream auto-scrolls to new turns smoothly.
